instruction: Posterior probability of being a mosaic mutation, ranging from 0 to 1. Higher value means the locus is more likely to be a true mosaic mutation based on Bayesian inference.
Variant allele frequency (VAF) of the mosaic allele, ranging from 0 to 1. Higher value may suggest germline or technical artifacts.

Variant allele frequency (VAF), ranging from 0 to 1. Values which are too low may suggest sequencing error or noise. But in snATAC-seq, a mutation with low VAF can still be regared as candidate true locus.
Depth of reads supporting the mutant allele, integer ≥ 0. Higher value increases confidence in the presence of the mosaic variant.
Total sequencing depth at the locus, integer ≥ 0. Higher depth improves detection reliability and genotyping accuracy.
Absolute mutant length of STR insertion or deletion, integer ≥ 0.
Estimated population allele frequency for mosaic events, ranging from 0 to 1. Lower values indicate rarer variants, consistent with somatic mosaicism; high values may suggest common polymorphisms.
Fraction of samples or cells where the same mutation recurs across individuals or loci, ranging from 0 to 1. Lower values reduce risk of batch effects or hypermutable site bias.
Proportion of uncallable reads in the locus, ranging from 0 to 1. High values suggest unreliable read mapping or other systematical artifacts.

Mutation type classification: 'homhet' or 'hethom', indicating mutation patterns that are relatively less error-prone, distinguishing from hethet (heterozygosity at the individual level, where completely different alleles appear within a cell).
Type of mutation: SNV (single nucleotide variant), Insertion, or Deletion. These are typical somatic mosaic event types. Complex variants may be excluded for simplicity and accuracy.
Number of cell types in which the mosaic mutation is detected, integer ≥ 0. A value of 1 restricts detection to only one cell type, reducing cross-contamination risks.
Number of mutant reads with no cell type annotation, integer ≥ 0. Lower is better; zero ensures all mutatnt reads have valid cell type annotation.
Number of mutant reads in cell with max mutant reads, integer ≥ 0. A value of 1 limits support to at most one unique molecule, reducing PCR duplicate bias.
Number of reads used in genotyping the mosaic variant, integer ≥ 0. Higher values improve genotyping confidence; threshold ensures sufficient data usage.
Ratio of off-target stutter artifacts, ranging from 0 to 1. Lower values indicate cleaner signal; high stutter increases false positive risk.
Number of mismatching bases in the mutation site, integer ≥ 0. Zero is ideal, indicating high alignment accuracy and low mis-mapping.
Mean base quality score of the mutant site, typically Phred-scaled from 0 to 40+. Higher values indicate higher confidence in base calling accuracy.
Mean mapping quality of all reads at the locus, Phred-scaled from 0 to 60. Higher values indicate more uniquely mapped reads and lower multi-mapping risk.
Mean mapping quality of mutant reads only, Phred-scaled 0 to 60. Higher values increase confidence that mutant reads are correctly mapped.
Average number of flanking sequencing errors (substitutions) per base pair in the region, typically 0 to 0.01. Lower values indicate cleaner genomic context; high values suggest error-prone regions.
Same as above but calculated only on mutant-supporting reads. Lower values suggest the mutation is not in a hypermutable or error-prone context.
